definitions.gloss: impudently clever; cunning; shrewd in an annoying way
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who is clever in a petty, irritating way — using small tricks or manipulations rather than genuine intelligence.

examples.japanese: {小賢|こざか}しい{真似|まね}はやめろ。
あの{子|こ}は{小賢|こざか}しいことを{言|い}う。
examples.english: That kid says annoyingly clever things.

examples.japanese: {小賢|こざか}しい{手段|しゅだん}で{人|ひと}を{騙|だま}そうとするやつは{信用|しんよう}できない。
examples.english: You can't trust someone who tries to fool people with petty cunning.

notes:
The prefix {小|こ} adds a diminutive, contemptuous nuance to {賢|かしこ}い (clever, smart). While {賢|かしこ}い is positive, {小賢|こざか}しい is always negative — it implies cleverness that is petty, irritating, or presumptuous.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小賢|こざか}しい{真似|まね}: petty tricks
- {小賢|こざか}しい{手段|しゅだん}: cunning methods
- {小賢|こざか}しいことを{言|い}う: to say annoyingly clever things
- {小賢|こざか}しい{子|こ}ども: a precociously clever child (pejorative)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {賢|かしこ}い: clever, smart — positive evaluation
- {狡|ずる}い: sly, cunning — focuses on unfair advantage
- {生意気|なまいき}: cheeky, impudent — focuses on disrespect toward superiors

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {小賢|こざか}しくなかったら
